nodes.label: Produce O₂ on the Moon
nodes.body:
# Lunar Oxygen Production

## Description

Produce oxygen from lunar resources to support sustained human presence on the Moon. Oxygen is required for life support and propellant.

## Sub-goals

- Demonstrate oxygen extraction at pilot scale
- Achieve TRL 6 by 2030

## Key Capabilities Required

- [[Capabilities/Produce Oxygen]]

## Stakeholders

- [[Organizations/ESA]]

## Notes

attachments.label: Power Supply Interruption
attachments.body:
# Power Supply Interruption

## Description

Loss or significant reduction of electrical power during the 14-day lunar night halts all ISRU operations and may cause irreversible damage to thermal systems held above ambient temperature.

## Probability

- [ ] Low
- [ ] Medium
- [x] High

## Impact

- [ ] Low
- [ ] Medium
- [x] High

## Root Causes

- Solar array failure (dust, meteorite impact, pointing error)
- Battery/RFC depletion during extended outage
- Fission Surface Power system fault
- Grid distribution fault isolating a subsystem

## Mitigation

- Redundant power generation (solar + RFC or solar + FSP)
- Graceful shutdown procedures for all ISRU processes on power loss
- Thermal battery for critical hold temperatures on reactors
- Load-shedding priority: life support > power > ISRU production

## Notes

This is a top-level system risk. [[Capabilities/Generate Power]] must be designed with N+1 redundancy.

attachments.label: Future application: closed-loop life support
attachments.body:
# Closed-Loop Life Support

## Description

Achieve a fully closed-loop life support system for a lunar habitat using only locally produced resources. Crew consume oxygen and water, waste is processed and recycled, with ISRU providing top-up for losses.

## Sub-goals

- Zero Earth-resupply of oxygen (100% local production)
- >95% water recovery and recycling rate
- Continuous power supply through lunar night

## Key Capabilities Required

- [[Capabilities/Produce Oxygen]]
- [[Capabilities/Extract Water Ice]]
- [[Capabilities/Generate Power]]

## Notes

This is the ultimate long-term goal of a self-sustaining lunar outpost. Requires all lower-tier capabilities to be operational and integrated.

nodes.label: Sustained Propellant Supply
nodes.body:
# Propellant Production

## Description

Produce sufficient LOX/LH2 propellant from lunar resources to refuel ascent vehicles and in-space depots, reducing Earth-launched propellant mass by >50%. This is the primary economic driver for lunar ISRU.

## Sub-goals

- Achieve production rate of ≥1 tonne propellant/month
- Demonstrate successful vehicle refuelling operations
- Validate propellant quality meets flight certification standards

## Stakeholders

- [[Organizations/ESA]]

## Notes

Realising this goal enables dramatic reduction in launch costs to the lunar surface and makes sustained human presence economically viable.

nodes.label: Surface Power Station
nodes.body:
# Generate Power

## Description

Capability to generate and distribute continuous electrical power at the lunar surface. Critical enabler for all thermal, electrochemical, and mechanical ISRU processes. Power interruption during the 14-day lunar night is a defining constraint.

## Power Source Options

- **Solar PV arrays** — lightweight, TRL 9, but limited to lunar day (~14 Earth days)
- **Fission Surface Power (FSP)** — continuous 10 kWe, works through night, TRL 5 (NASA/DoE development)
- **RFC (Regenerative Fuel Cells)** — store solar energy as H₂/O₂, discharge at night

## Required Capability

- Continuous power: >10 kWe (ISRU operations)
- Peak power: >30 kWe (electrolysis + heating combined loads)
- Distribution: 480V DC or 100–120V bus

## Key Challenges

- 14-day lunar night with no solar input
- Dust accumulation on solar panels reduces output
- Thermal management of waste heat in vacuum

## Risks

- [[Risks/Power Supply Interruption]]
- [[Risks/Dust Contamination]]

## Notes

nodes.label: Lunar Regolith Feedstock
nodes.body:
# Regolith

## Description

Lunar surface soil and crushed rock. The primary feedstock for ISRU on the Moon.

## Source / Location

Lunar surface — mare and highland regions.

## Availability

Abundant across the lunar surface. Composition varies by region.

## Composition / Properties

- Oxide content: ~40-45% oxygen by mass (bound in oxides)
- Primary minerals: pyroxene, plagioclase, olivine, ilmenite
- Grain size: typically 40-800 µm

## Used By

- [[Technologies/Hydrogen Reduction]]
- [[Technologies/Molten Regolith Electrolysis]]

## Notes

nodes.label: Extracted Water
nodes.body: Water recovered from polar ice deposits and regolith processing. Feedstock for electrolysis (oxygen + hydrogen) and a life-support reserve.

nodes.label: Hydrogen Supply
nodes.body: Hydrogen produced by water electrolysis. Reductant for the ilmenite reduction loop and fuel component of LOX/LH₂ propellant.

nodes.label: Oxygen Supply
nodes.body: Oxygen extracted from regolith or water — breathing gas for crewed operations and oxidizer for propellant. The central product of this roadmap: three competing production routes feed it.

nodes.label: Regolith Excavation
nodes.body:
# Regolith Excavation

## Description

Mechanical excavation and transport of lunar regolith for use as ISRU feedstock. Covers bucket-wheel, auger screw, and pneumatic conveying concepts adapted for lunar gravity and vacuum.

## Inputs

- Electrical power
- Excavation hardware

## Outputs

- Regolith (bulk feed stream)

## Parameters

- Excavation rate: 100–500 kg/hr (pilot scale)
- Depth: 0–2 m (surface layer, primary target)
- Power (kW): 0.5–3 (per kg excavated)
- Dust generation: high — mitigation required

## Key Challenges

- Highly abrasive regolith causes rapid tool wear
- Vacuum operation — no air cooling or pneumatic actuation
- Cohesive regolith at depth can jam auger mechanisms
- Electrostatic adhesion of fine particles to surfaces

## TRL Justification

Multiple auger and bucket-wheel prototypes demonstrated in lunar simulant at Earth gravity. Vacuum and low-gravity testing still limited.

## Key Experiments

- [[Experiments/Regolith Auger Demonstration]]

## Risks

- [[Risks/Equipment Wear]]
- [[Risks/Dust Contamination]]

## Notes

Enables downstream processing by [[Technologies/Water Ice Extraction]] for PSR targets and feeds bulk regolith to thermal reduction technologies.

attachments.label: Regolith Auger Demonstration
attachments.body:
# Regolith Auger Demonstration

## Description

Ground-based demonstration of an auger-screw excavation system in a vacuum chamber filled with JSC-1A lunar simulant. Characterises excavation rate, tool wear, dust generation, and power consumption under representative conditions.

## Objective

Establish excavation performance vs tool geometry and rotation speed; measure wear rate on different auger materials; quantify dust lofting inside the chamber.

## Methodology

1. Compact JSC-1A simulant to target bulk density (1.5 g/cm³ surface, 1.9 g/cm³ at 0.5 m depth)
2. Run auger at 3 rotation speeds × 2 penetration rates — 6 test points
3. Extract at 20 cm, 50 cm, 100 cm depth; measure accumulated regolith per pass
4. Weigh auger before and after for wear measurement
5. Particle counter monitors dust during all runs

## Success Criteria

- Excavation rate > 10 kg/hr at lab scale
- Tool mass loss < 1 g per 10 kg excavated
- No chamber contamination beyond accepted dust threshold

## Required Infrastructure

- Lunar Simulant Testbed (vacuum chamber + regolith bed + instrumentation)

## Risks

- [[Risks/Dust Contamination]]
- [[Risks/Equipment Wear]]

## Notes

attachments.label: Equipment Wear
attachments.body:
# Equipment Wear

## Description

Severe abrasion of mechanical components (auger teeth, seals, conveyor belts, valve seats) caused by the angular, glass-like particles in lunar regolith. Wear rates significantly exceed terrestrial analogues due to the lack of water-rounded particle edges.

## Probability

- [ ] Low
- [x] Medium
- [ ] High

## Impact

- [ ] Low
- [x] Medium
- [ ] High

## Root Causes

- Regolith particle angularity (no erosional rounding)
- High hardness of ilmenite and pyroxene grains
- No lubrication possible in vacuum (conventional lubricants outgas)

## Mitigation

- Ceramic or tungsten-carbide coated tool surfaces
- Dry lubricants (MoS₂, PTFE-impregnated bearings) validated for vacuum
- Modular/replaceable wear elements — design for field swap
- Condition monitoring (vibration, current draw) to detect wear onset

## Notes

Works synergistically with [[Risks/Dust Contamination]] — fine abrasive dust generated by excavation causes secondary wear on seals and optical surfaces downstream.

nodes.label: Water Ice Extraction
nodes.body:
# Water Ice Extraction

## Description

Extraction and sublimation of water ice from permanently shadowed regions (PSRs) near the lunar poles. Ice-bearing regolith is excavated and thermally processed to drive off water vapour, which is then captured and condensed.

## Inputs

- Ice-bearing regolith (PSR deposits)
- Thermal energy for sublimation
- Excavation capability ([[Technologies/Regolith Excavation]])

## Outputs

- Water (liquid, for electrolysis or life support)

## Parameters

- Water content (mass %): 0.1–10% (estimates vary widely by site)
- Extraction temperature: −100°C to 0°C (sublimation regime)
- Power (kW): 1–5 (heating and transport)

## Key Challenges

- PSRs are permanently dark — no solar power available locally
- Very low temperatures require robust thermal control
- Water ice distribution is heterogeneous; exact deposits poorly mapped
- High excavation rate needed to compensate for low ice concentration

## TRL Justification

Concept studies and laboratory demonstrations on ice-simulant mixtures exist, but no integrated system tested under representative thermal/vacuum conditions.

## Key Experiments

None planned yet.

## Risks

- [[Risks/Equipment Wear]]
- [[Risks/Dust Contamination]]
- [[Risks/Power Supply Interruption]]

## Notes

Produces water that feeds [[Technologies/Water Electrolysis]], enabling the hydrogen-oxygen cycle.

nodes.label: Water Electrolysis
nodes.body:
# Water Electrolysis

## Description

Electrochemical splitting of water into hydrogen and oxygen using an electrical current. Produces hydrogen for use as a reductant in hydrogen reduction processes and oxygen as a direct ISRU product. Well-established terrestrially; lunar adaptation requires operation under vacuum and low-gravity conditions.

## Inputs

- Water (liquid or from melted ice)
- Electrical power (solar or nuclear)

## Outputs

- Hydrogen (recycled back to Hydrogen Reduction reactor)
- Oxygen (collected and compressed)

## Parameters

- Power (kW): 1–5 (lab scale)
- Efficiency (%): 70–85 (energy to hydrogen)
- Operating temperature: 50–80°C (PEM), 700–900°C (SOEC)
- Pressure: 1–30 bar

## Technology Variants

- **PEM (Proton Exchange Membrane)** — compact, fast response, TRL 8+ on Earth
- **SOEC (Solid Oxide Electrolysis Cell)** — higher efficiency at elevated temperature, better suited to co-electrolysis of CO₂+H₂O

## TRL Justification

PEM electrolysis is TRL 9 on Earth. Lunar adaptation (vacuum operation, reduced gravity, regolith-contaminated water input) brings effective TRL to 5.

## Key Experiments

- [[Experiments/Water Electrolysis Bench Test]]

## Notes

Hydrogen produced here feeds the [[Technologies/Hydrogen Reduction]] process, closing the reagent loop.

attachments.label: Electrolysis Efficiency Data
attachments.body:
# Electrolysis Efficiency Data

## Description

Faradaic efficiency, gas purity, and membrane degradation results from the Water Electrolysis Bench Test campaign. Provides quantitative support for the PEM electrolysis approach in lunar ISRU contexts.

## Source Experiment

- [[Experiments/Water Electrolysis Bench Test]]

## Key Findings

- Peak Faradaic efficiency: 94.2% at 0.8 A/cm²
- O₂ purity: 99.7% at nominal operating point; drops to 98.1% at maximum current
- Membrane conductivity loss: 3.8% after 100-hour run with mineral-doped water
- Operating regime confirmed: 0.5–1.2 A/cm² balances efficiency and longevity

## Confidence Level

Medium — bench scale, Earth gravity, controlled inlet water chemistry

## Implications

Confirms PEM electrolysis viability for ISRU hydrogen supply. Recommends upstream water purification step to protect membrane lifetime. Supports hydrogen production rate estimates for [[Technologies/Hydrogen Reduction]] mass balance.

## Notes

attachments.label: Water Electrolysis Bench Test
attachments.body:
# Water Electrolysis Bench Test

## Description

Bench-scale demonstration of PEM water electrolysis under simulated lunar operating conditions: low-pressure inlet water, variable load profile, and characterisation of membrane degradation with regolith-contaminated water.

## Objective

Measure Faradaic efficiency and gas purity at varying current densities and water quality levels; quantify membrane degradation rate from dissolved minerals in ISRU-derived water.

## Methodology

1. Deionised baseline run at rated current — establish reference efficiency
2. Introduce mineral-doped water (matching simulated ISRU water chemistry)
3. Step current density from 0.1 to 2.0 A/cm²; measure H₂/O₂ flow and purity
4. 100-hour endurance run at design point; inspect membrane post-test

## Success Criteria

- Faradaic efficiency > 90% at design current density
- O₂ purity > 99.5% throughout
- Membrane shows <5% conductivity loss after 100 hours

## Required Infrastructure

- [[Infrastructure/Vacuum Furnace]] (for low-pressure water pre-treatment)
- Electrolysis Test Rig (PEM stack, power supply, gas analyser)

## Risks

- [[Risks/Insufficient Heating Efficiency]]

## Notes

Results feed directly into [[Technologies/Water Electrolysis]] TRL assessment and inform water purification requirements for ISRU systems.

nodes.label: Hydrogen Reduction (Ilmenite)
nodes.body:
# Hydrogen Reduction

## Description

Reduction of iron oxides in lunar regolith using hydrogen at elevated temperatures. Produces water which is then electrolyzed to yield oxygen and recycle hydrogen.

## Inputs

- Regolith (ilmenite-rich preferred)
- Hydrogen (recycled)

## Outputs

- Oxygen
- Water (intermediate)

## Parameters

- Power (kW): 5-10 (lab scale)
- Temperature: 900-1100°C
- Yield (%): 5-15 (oxygen extraction from bulk regolith)
- Complexity: Medium

## TRL Justification

Demonstrated in laboratory with simulated regolith. Multiple research groups have achieved 5-15% oxygen yield.

## Key Experiments

- [[Experiments/Vacuum Chamber Pyrolysis Test]]

## Risks

- [[Risks/Insufficient Heating Efficiency]]

## Notes

# Laboratory Results

## Description

Mass spectrometry data and yield calculations from vacuum chamber pyrolysis tests on JSC-1A lunar simulant.

## Source Experiment

- [[Experiments/Vacuum Chamber Pyrolysis Test]]

2025-03-15

attachments.label: Vacuum Chamber Pyrolysis Test
attachments.body:
# Vacuum Chamber Pyrolysis Test

## Description

Laboratory-scale demonstration of hydrogen reduction of lunar regolith simulant under vacuum conditions.

## Objective

Measure oxygen yield from hydrogen reduction of JSC-1A lunar simulant at varying temperatures.

## Methodology

1. Load simulant into vacuum furnace
2. Heat to target temperature under vacuum
3. Introduce hydrogen flow
4. Measure off-gas composition via mass spectrometry

## Success Criteria

- Oxygen yield > 5%
- Reproducible across 5 runs

## Required Infrastructure

- [[Infrastructure/Vacuum Furnace]]

## Expected Evidence

- Gas composition data
- Yield vs temperature curves
- Material characterization of residue

## Risks

- [[Risks/Insufficient Heating Efficiency]]

## Notes

# Molten Regolith Electrolysis

## Description

Direct electrolysis of molten regolith to produce oxygen at the anode and metal alloys at the cathode. Eliminates the need for consumable reactants.

- Regolith
- Electrical power

## Outputs

- Oxygen

## Parameters

- Temperature: 1500-1700°C
- Yield (%): 20-30 (oxygen extraction)
- Complexity: High

## TRL Justification

Demonstrated in laboratory at small scale. Challenges remain with electrode degradation and melt management.

## Key Experiments

- [[Experiments/Vacuum Chamber Pyrolysis Test]]

nodes.label: Carbothermal Reduction
nodes.body:
# Carbothermal Reduction

## Description

High-temperature reduction of regolith oxides using carbon or methane as a reductant. Produces CO gas which is then disproportionated (Boudouard reaction) or oxidised to recover oxygen and recycle carbon. Offers an alternative reagent loop that does not require a hydrogen supply.

## Inputs

- Regolith (bulk feedstock)
- Carbon or methane (recycled reductant)
- High-power microwave or concentrated solar heating

## Outputs

- Oxygen (primary product)
- Silicon carbide / metal alloys (secondary)
- Carbon monoxide (intermediate, recycled)

## Parameters

- Operating temperature: 1600–2000°C
- Power (kW): 15–30 (lab scale)
- Oxygen yield (%): 15–25

## Key Challenges

- Extremely high temperatures demand refractory containment materials
- Carbon loss through SiC formation reduces cycle efficiency
- Process control at lunar temperatures is complex

## TRL Justification

Proof-of-concept demonstrations with methane and simulant in laboratory. Significant engineering challenges remain before pilot-scale testing.

## Risks

- [[Risks/Insufficient Heating Efficiency]]

## Notes

Competes with [[Technologies/Hydrogen Reduction]] and [[Technologies/Molten Regolith Electrolysis]] as an independent pathway that avoids dependence on water-derived hydrogen.

nodes.label: Cryogenic Storage & Liquefaction
nodes.body:
# Cryogenic Propellant Storage

## Description

Liquefaction, storage, and transfer of oxygen (LOX) and hydrogen (LH2) produced from lunar ISRU operations. The lunar thermal environment — extreme day/night cycles and vacuum — poses unique challenges for cryogenic fluid management with minimal boil-off.

## Inputs

- Gaseous oxygen from ISRU processes
- Gaseous hydrogen from water electrolysis
- Electrical power for compression and refrigeration

## Outputs

- Liquid Oxygen (LOX) at −183°C
- Liquid Hydrogen (LH2) at −253°C

## Parameters

- Storage pressure: 3–10 bar (subcooled LOX), 2–5 bar (slush LH2)
- Boil-off rate target: <0.1%/day with active refrigeration
- Power (kW): 5–15 (liquefaction and active cooling)

## Key Challenges

- Achieving near-zero boil-off on a body with no convective cooling
- Thermal cycling from 14-day lunar day/night
- Seals and valves rated for cryogenic vacuum service
- Long-term material compatibility under radiation exposure

## TRL Justification

LOX storage well-studied; LH2 at this scale in lunar environment is TRL 3. Active zero-boil-off demonstrations planned for Gateway.

## Risks

- [[Risks/Power Supply Interruption]]

## Notes

Bridges the gap between ISRU gas production ([[Capabilities/Produce Oxygen]]) and flight-ready propellant loading ([[Goals/Propellant Production]]).

- [ ] Medium
- [x] High

## Root Causes

- Solar array failure (dust, meteorite impact, pointing error)
- Battery/RFC depletion during extended outage
- Fission Surface Power system fault
- Grid distribution fault isolating a subsystem

## Mitigation

- Redundant power generation (solar + RFC or solar + FSP)
- Graceful shutdown procedures for all ISRU processes on power loss
- Thermal battery for critical hold temperatures on reactors
- Load-shedding priority: life support > power > ISRU production

## Notes

This is a top-level system risk. [[Capabilities/Generate Power]] must be designed with N+1 redundancy.
